To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the ψ‐CD effect can be described as an enhanced CD of delocalized excitations of DNA, (b) the enhancement is not limited to the size of the system, and (c) the enhancement is broken by disorder.

(i) a generalized transition dipole coupling approach for the calculation of CD spectra of large molecular aggregates has been developed and applied to the study of DNA condensation; (ii) the origin of the CD enhancement observed upon DNA condensation is primarily caused by the delocalization of phonon‐like vibrations; and (iii) small structural irregularities allow for the enhancement, but a larger disorder breaks the enhancement.
(1) the ψ-effect is caused by delocalization of the excitations in the DNA strand, and (2) the size of the system that exhibits the effect is not limited by the wavelength of light.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new theoretical model of the circular dichroism enhancement (ψ‐effect) in large DNA aggregates.
the development of the transition dipole model of CD spectroscopy to describe the CD enhancement in large molecular aggregates.
the development and application of a novel approach to the modeling of the CD spectra of large molecular systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ψ‐effect originates from the collective excitations of the nucleic acids.
the CD enhancement in large DNA systems is caused by the delocalized excitations in nucleotide strands and is not related to the size of the system.
the CD enhancement originates from the coupling of electronic transitions of nucleic acid bases to the delocalized excitations of the entire DNA aggregate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ψ‐CD effect is caused by the delocalized excitations in nucleotides, which are enhanced in large aggregates due to the increased number of nucleotides.
it is now possible to model the circular dichroism enhancement phenomenon in large nucleic acid aggregates, and to relate it to their structural features.
the ψ‐CD enhancement is caused by a delocalized excitation, and that this excitation does not necessarily need to be of electronic origin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple and computationally inexpensive model is sufficient to understand the origin and the size of the system where the ψ‐CD effect is observed.
the ψ‐effect is a general property of large molecular aggregates and is not limited to DNA condensates.
the CD signal can be enhanced in systems of arbitrary size, and the effect does not require a large system.
